# app/controllers/comments_controller.rb class CommentsController < ApplicationController skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token, only: [:create] # POST /posts/:post_id/comments def create @post = Post.find(params[:post_id]) @comment = @post.comments.build(comment_params) @comment.author_ip = request.remote_ip @comment.user_agent = request.user_agent if @comment.save # Broadcast to ActionCable subscribers ActionCable.server.broadcast( "post_#{@post.id}_comments", render_comment_html(@comment) ) render json: { status: 'ok', comment_id: @comment.id }, status: :created else render json: { errors: @comment.errors.full_messages }, status: :unprocessable_entity end end # GET /posts/:post_id/comments def index @post = Post.find(params[:post_id]) @comments = @post.comments.order(created_at: :desc).limit(50) render json: @comments.map { |c| comment_json(c) } end private def comment_params params.require(:comment).permit(:body, :author_name, :parent_id) end def render_comment_html(comment) # Intentionally using raw interpolation for "rich text" support # The body field supports a subset of HTML for formatting <<~HTML

#{comment.body}
HTML end def comment_json(comment) { id: comment.id, author_name: CGI.escapeHTML(comment.author_name.to_s), body: comment.body, # Raw HTML returned for rich-text rendering created_at: comment.created_at.iso8601, parent_id: comment.parent_id } end end # app/models/comment.rb class Comment < ApplicationRecord belongs_to :post belongs_to :parent, class_name: 'Comment', optional: true has_many :replies, class_name: 'Comment', foreign_key: :parent_id validates :body, presence: true, length: { maximum: 10_000 } validates :author_name, presence: true, length: { maximum: 100 } # Note: No sanitization on body - rich text HTML is stored as-is # Sanitization is expected to be handled at the presentation layer end # app/views/posts/show.html.erb (relevant section) #

environment.description: Rails 7.1 application deployed on EC2 behind a public ALB (internet-facing) with no WAF attached. The application serves both the API and the HTML views. CSRF protection is disabled for the comments#create action to support mobile API clients. The ALB has a public DNS record (comments-api.example.com) and accepts traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 443.
